scope.execution_method: Committed API execution plus deterministic DITA, repository-command, configuration, update, diagnostics, production-boundary, and six-locale parity simulation.
scope.honesty_rule: Source-install procedures cannot pass from static command presence alone. Missing exact operating-system releases, five-distribution command sequences, documentation-build steps, rollback or stop conditions, or hands-on/simulation transcripts remain release blockers.

normalization.rule: Each section_reviews entry expands to one protocol review item for every topic_id in topic_ids. Task fields resolve from the localized DITA task body; concept claims resolve from title, shortdesc, conbody, and related links.

field_resolution.task_or_claim: section.task_or_claim plus the localized topic title/shortdesc
field_resolution.prerequisites: task/taskbody/prereq for tasks; section.prerequisites for concepts
field_resolution.exact_steps: task/taskbody/steps/step/cmd in document order for tasks; section.exact_steps for concepts
field_resolution.expected_result: task/taskbody/result for tasks; section.expected_result for concepts

section_reviews.task_or_claim: An administrator can prepare, install, configure, start, and verify BPM from a Linux source checkout.
section_reviews.prerequisites: A named Linux distribution/release, Python 3.14+, Git, build tooling, curl, repository access, and an isolated target database.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Five localized target topics now provide exact package/Python, guarded checkout, virtual environment, editable install, migration, documentation build, foreground start, probe/UI, log, and stop-boundary commands.
section_reviews.expected_result: A source-run process answers /health and /health/ready and serves /profiles after migration; authoring is complete, but execution remains unverified per selected distribution until BPM091-M6-06.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: An administrator can run the Linux source workflow inside WSL 2 and verify access from Windows without inferring native-Windows support.
section_reviews.prerequisites: Windows 10 or 11, WSL 2, a named Ubuntu LTS release, PowerShell, a WSL shell, repository access, and permission to install prerequisites.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Current topics provide WSL setup, apt prerequisites, Linux-filesystem checkout, environment, migration, process start, Linux/PowerShell probes, and networking recovery, but do not name an exact Ubuntu release or include a complete docs-build and rollback transcript.
section_reviews.expected_result: BPM runs inside WSL and responds from both WSL and Windows; this remains simulated rather than evidenced on an exact host/release pair.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: Operators can identify effective configuration, storage, logs, backup evidence, network exposure, CORS, and unsupported operational capabilities.
section_reviews.prerequisites: A source-run instance and access to its BPM_* configuration, working directory, foreground logs, data path, and documentation path.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Review configuration sources, inventory persistent and generated paths, assess bind/CORS exposure, and record supported and deferred boundaries.
section_reviews.expected_result: An operational record identifies current settings and evidence without claiming managed secrets, service packaging, reverse proxy, TLS, backup automation, or HA support.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: Operators can update a source checkout with pre-change evidence, guarded dependency refresh, forward migrations, documentation checks, probes, and explicit rollback stop conditions.
section_reviews.prerequisites: A running source checkout, approved target ref, clean or understood worktree, stopped process, database backup, export evidence, and previous revision.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Record revision/configuration, back up data, export critical profiles, fetch and checkout the approved ref, reinstall dependencies, run tests/migrations/docs, restart, probe, and stop rather than assume database downgrade safety.
section_reviews.expected_result: The update either reaches a verified source-run state or stops at a documented boundary without destructive rollback assumptions.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: Integrators can select a supported synchronous HTTP pattern and understand current OpenAPI, concurrency, authentication, retry, webhook, and runtime-enforcement boundaries.
section_reviews.prerequisites: An integration owner, BPM base URL, current OpenAPI document, and an external audit/retry policy.
exact_steps: Identify the integration audience and ownership boundary.
Apply API conventions and stop at explicit limitations before implementing downstream behavior.
section_reviews.expected_result: The integration design uses only current BPM API guarantees and keeps unsupported orchestration outside BPM.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: An integrating product can read and update profiles safely, manage retirement, and validate/import/export Firefox policies JSON.
section_reviews.prerequisites: A reachable BPM instance, current OpenAPI, schema channel, deterministic profile identity/revision, and synthetic policies.json input.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Execute documented profile lifecycle, validation, import, export, archive/restore, and conflict paths with the stated content types and response states.
section_reviews.expected_result: API responses and exported Firefox documents match current FastAPI behavior without bypassing revision, validation, or lifecycle controls.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: Integrators can gate work on current probes and execute representative pull/compare/update and import/review/export workflows.
section_reviews.prerequisites: A test BPM instance, base URL, known profiles or synthetic input, and an external record for retries and audit evidence.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Call liveness/readiness, execute the selected end-to-end scenario, preserve statuses/revisions/hashes, and handle documented failure boundaries.
section_reviews.expected_result: The scenario reaches the documented API state while probes remain a minimal handshake rather than dependency diagnostics.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: A control product can pull inventory, validate before update, hand off import/review/export, gate startup, and retain failure evidence.
section_reviews.prerequisites: A deterministic test instance, current schema channel, external control-product state, and a policy for retries, idempotency, and audit retention.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Run each control-product sequence against current endpoints and preserve request, response, revision, status, and decision evidence.
section_reviews.expected_result: The external product can complete or safely stop each orchestration without relying on undocumented BPM queues, webhooks, authentication, or audit storage.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: Operators can classify startup/probe, schema, import/export, storage, WSL, and documentation-portal failures and stop before unsafe recovery.
section_reviews.prerequisites: The failing command, source revision, non-secret configuration names, response status/body, relevant paths/checksums, and sanitized logs.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Reproduce with the smallest probe or focused test, classify the owning layer, preserve evidence, use documented recovery, and stop before direct database/generated-output edits or unsupported rollback.
section_reviews.expected_result: The operator reaches a bounded diagnosis and either restores the documented workflow or records a safe escalation package.

section_reviews.task_or_claim: Maintainers can assess current single-node source operation and explicitly separate preparation evidence from deferred production capabilities.
section_reviews.prerequisites: Completed source-operation, configuration, storage, network, update, probe, and backup/export evidence reviews.
section_reviews.exact_steps: Assess single-node evidence, review exposure and proxy questions, plan monitoring/backup/update windows, and record deferred HA, TLS/proxy, managed-secret, rolling-upgrade, and restore boundaries.
section_reviews.expected_result: The record describes current source operation without claiming production readiness or support for deferred topology and automation features.

release_blockers.finding: BPM091-M6-06 validates syntax, ordering, shared CPython integrity, and Ubuntu 26.04 runtime behavior, and records deterministic simulations for the other four targets. No target yet has a complete clean-host transcript from package installation through stop verification.
release_blockers.closure_evidence: docs/architecture/linux-source-install-validation-0.9.1.json must be updated with five clean-target passes before release.
release_blockers.release_rule: Do not claim Administrator source-install sufficiency while the validation report has release_ready=false. WSL must reuse or name the validated Ubuntu LTS sequence and retain Windows/WSL-specific probe evidence.

release_blockers.finding: Administrator DITA metadata and visible source-deployment/update wording still identify BPM 0.9.0 while this review targets BPM 0.9.1.
missing_evidence: absence of stale 0.9.0 Administrator portal instructions
release_blockers.release_rule: Behavioral simulations may remain useful, but the 0.9.1 portal cannot ship these topics until version wording is refreshed and locale parity gates pass.

linux_source_install_validation.result_summary: 19 passed; Ubuntu 26.04 runtime/migration/probes/UI/stop and CPython 3.14.6 checksum passed; four targets remain simulation-only.

linux_source_install_authoring.result_summary: 282 passed; make docs-validate and make docs-build also passed for all six locales.
linux_source_install_authoring.boundary: Static authoring, DITA publication, links, metadata, and repository behavior are verified. Distribution execution belongs to BPM091-M6-06.

summary.result: Current operations, update, health, troubleshooting, integration, and production-boundary procedures agree with repository behavior under deterministic simulation. Source-install evidence and 0.9.1 version wording remain explicit release blockers.

unverified_boundaries: No clean-host Linux distribution or Windows/WSL installation was executed during this review.
The health and readiness endpoints prove only the current application responses, not database dependency detail, production topology, or service-level readiness.
No production reverse proxy, TLS termination, service manager, managed secret store, HA cluster, rolling upgrade, or automated restore behavior is claimed or verified.
Database downgrade safety is not guaranteed; update recovery must stop at the documented backup and source-reference boundaries.
